document.title: Chen Lab — Relative Risk Across Heat Exposure Quintiles: Third Trimester
document.source: YSPH Environmental Epidemiology Lab — Preprint v2 (not peer reviewed)
document.ambi_context: Dose-response visualization data — third trimester heat exposure by income stratum

chart_config.x_axis: Heat exposure quintile (extreme heat days in third trimester)
chart_config.y_axis: Relative risk of preterm birth (ref = Q1 exposure, no extreme heat days)
chart_config.note: Quintile 1 = 0–1 extreme heat days; Quintile 5 = 9+ extreme heat days during third trimester

data_points.label: Q5 (9+ days)
data_points.note: ⚠ AC confounder under review for low-income Q5 — central estimate may shift; lower bound (1.24) considered stable

key_finding.summary: Diverging dose-response curves by income stratum. Low-income tracts show a steep, monotonic increase in RR with heat exposure. Higher-income tracts show a flatter, attenuated curve — consistent with AC access buffering effect.
key_finding.policy_implication: Pattern holds under conservative assumptions. Supports pilot program targeting low-income tracts with highest heat exposure days.
